name: Warren G. Harding
role: U.S. senator from Ohio (1915-1921) and 29th U.S. president (1921-1923)
summary: Harding was a Republican party man who ran on a return to normalcy, meaning lower taxes, protective tariffs, balanced budgets, less government interference in business and no entanglement in a League of Nations. He supported women's suffrage, arms limitation and disarmament by conference, and restricted immigration, and in 1921 he called for political and educational opportunity for black Americans while rejecting social equality and favouring separation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called for less government interference with business and an end to government experiments in business, and presented the existing private system as the base to build on.

public-ownership.rationale: Called government operation of the railways, the wartime experiment, a supreme folly and said it did not offer the cure; asked for an end to government experiments in business.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Urged lower income tax rates and an end to the excess-profits tax, with the Mellon programme; he accepted a compromise bill with higher rates than Mellon wanted.

unions-good.rationale: Said labor's right to organize is as fundamental as capital's, but also wanted unions regulated and strikes replaced by tribunals, so the evidence is mixed.

strong-leader.rationale: Said executive powers were already too large, disavowed any wish to enlarge them and promised no dictation of Congress, preferring cooperation with the legislature.

state-harmful.rationale: Called representative government the highest expression and surest guaranty of liberty and civilization.

decide-locally.rationale: Held that schooling is best left to local communities, yet asked for federal action on education of immigrants, child labor and prohibition enforcement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pledged to hold fast to the American inheritance and called for magnifying the national viewpoint and the Americanizing of newcomers.

gradual-change.rationale: Argued for restoration over revolution, adjustment over agitation and experiment, and said wild experiment would only add confusion while the proven system should be administered efficiently.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Signed the 1921 quota act, welcomed restriction of immigration in his Birmingham speech and said quotas should not be enlarged before aliens were registered and examined abroad.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Declared a world super-government contrary to everything Americans cherish, and rejected the League as negotiated.

free-trade.rationale: Pressed for a permanent protective tariff to preserve domestic industry and employment and signed the Fordney-McCumber Act.

nation-first.rationale: Preferred sustainment in triumphant nationality to submergence in internationality and said tranquility at home mattered more than peace abroad, while still favouring conferences.

revolution-justified.rationale: Called for restoration, not revolution, and denounced advocates of revolution abusing American hospitality.

central-planning.rationale: Asked for an end to government experiments in business and rejected wild experiments with the economic system.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Urged a permanent tariff to safeguard productive activity and employment, signed Fordney-McCumber and called for flexible rates to guard American industry.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended government by competing political parties and wished the South not to be solidly of one party.

democracy-best.rationale: Called representative popular government the highest expression and surest guaranty of liberty and said democracy is the ideal political state.

direct-votes.rationale: Described the system as representative popular government carried on through parties, with Congress making law.

right-to-secede.rationale: Praised the maintenance of the union and the supremacy of the Nation after the Civil War.

war-builds-character.rationale: Condemned war's cost and sorrows and hoped to outlaw it, though he also praised wartime industrial resourcefulness.

military-superiority.rationale: Hosted the Washington Conference, which agreed to limit naval armaments, and asked for less preparation for war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Spoke of the nation as made of many origins whose oneness is above group lines, but also backed quota restriction favouring older stock.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Said capital and labor are often the same person and condemned demagogues who array class against class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said equal opportunity had been attained, and that Providence gave men unequal capacities so equal results never follow.

restore-past-order.rationale: Called for restoration, yet said the old order would not return and that the country should go on as well as preserve.

direct-action.rationale: Held that strikes, lockouts and boycotts are out of place in an industrial society and wanted revolution rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Refused to recognize Soviet Russia or tolerate its propaganda and rejected revolutionary experiments.

conscription.rationale: Described an ideal of every man and woman called under the flag for service in war and renewed that call for a universal draft in his second annual message.

total-state.rationale: Warned that people expect too much of government, wanted less interference and government out of business.

national-rebirth.rationale: Wanted a return to normalcy rather than radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said the United States covets no conquest, has no territorial greed and seeks nothing which is another's.

bound-labor.rationale: Counted the elimination of slavery and serfdom among the advances of American society.

universal-morality.rationale: Said liberty and justice are the unquestioned possession of all peoples and inherent rights are of God.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Promoted balanced budgets and rigid economies as remedies and opposed an unfunded soldiers' bonus.

class-collaboration.rationale: Urged conciliation, common counsel and arbitration between capital and labor and an industrial peace based on mutual interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Said racial pride would bring natural segregation without narrowing any rights, which implies it need not be imposed by law; no call for segregation laws.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said the fundamental law recognizes no class, group or section.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Praised the leasing of coal, oil and gas lands on a royalty basis; the Teapot Dome leases were made under his administration.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Called for making the alien respect American institutions, magnifying the American viewpoint to those seeking citizenship and Americanizing immigrants.

national-mission.rationale: Offered America as an example, but sought no part in directing the destinies of the Old World.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Asked Congress for farm credit, reclamation, federal aid for roads and education and railway regulation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Said racial amalgamation there cannot be and endorsed each race preserving its own racial purity and pride.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said black citizens should have all the rights of others and fair treatment, but he also held to an inescapable racial difference.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the success of popular government rests on the deliberate popular will.

separated-powers.rationale: Pledged to restore cooperation between executive and Congress, disclaiming encroachment on its functions.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Proposed that labor tribunal rulings be binding in essential public services and that strikes not be timed to paralyze them.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Believed the party in power should settle policy in conference and then adhere to it, subject to the good of the Republic.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said every commitment must be made in the exercise of national sovereignty and refused a super-government.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said America could be a party to no permanent military alliance.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Hoped for a redistribution of population toward smaller country communities and lamented the drift from farm to city.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Backed relief appropriations for Russian famine, but said America would not assume burdens that other nations must bear.

collective-defense.rationale: Opposed commitments that bind the United States to armed alliance and, as senator, objected to the League covenant's Article X.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Said government runs through parties and he expected the party in power to take responsibility.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Treated the Civil War outcome, union maintained and the Nation supreme, as the removal of the Constitution's one ambiguity.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Called for respect for law and said the executive should not be enlarged; urged every person to abide by the law.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Rejected commercial and industrial exclusion and aloofness, saying a nation must buy where it sells.

patriotic-education.rationale: Called for education of newcomers toward Americanization and magnification of the national viewpoint.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Pressed for the Budget system under which the executive budget goes to Congress, and said Congress's sanction must accompany policy.

democratic-peace.rationale: Believed that when governments establish a freedom like America's the last sorrow of international warfare would be written.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Said contempt for law, even prohibition law that is thought to restrict personal liberty, will ultimately destroy the Republic.

non-intervention.rationale: Criticized Wilson's intervention in Haiti and the Dominican Republic and disclaimed dictating to others, but kept troops in several countries.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Insisted on commitments within national sovereignty, yet favored a world court for justiciable disputes.

religion-illusion.rationale: Stated belief in divine inspiration of the founders and God's intent in the Republic.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Said inherent rights are of God and the founders were divinely inspired, but placed governmental success on the popular will.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Sought less armament consistent with national necessities, not abolition, and wanted universal service in defense.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pledged non-involvement in Old World affairs and no entangling alliance.

racial-franchise.rationale: Said the black man should vote when fit and that political rights need not differ by race, opposing race-based franchise limits.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Warned against group and class organizations and denounced demagogues who array group against group, and urged black voters to divide between parties.

racial-pride.rationale: Urged the inculcating of race pride and ambition in the black community and said pride in one's race is the way to natural separation.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Said America never made offensive warfare and wished offensive war to be outlawed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Said women's intuitions, refinements and intelligence would exalt the social order.

arms-reduction.rationale: Convened the Washington Conference and called for real limitation of armament and less preparation for war.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Condemned slackerism and treason in wartime and called for universal service.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Said labor has the right to deal with its problems through chosen agents, while also proposing mediation tribunals.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Defended the constitutional machinery and its efficient administration, opposing advocates of revolution.

farm-price-support.rationale: Backed expanded federal farm credit, cooperative marketing and emergency tariffs for agriculture, though denying legislation could cure price swings.

women-suffrage.rationale: Voted for the Nineteenth Amendment as senator and called on women to exercise the full privileges of citizenship.

race-social-construct.rationale: Described racial difference as fundamental, eternal and inescapable.

equal-conscription.rationale: Pictured every man and woman called under the flag for military or civic service.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Held that parties are the governing agencies of representative government and said he would ever have it so.

notes: Harding died in 1923, so answers rest on his own speeches and his record in office. His Birmingham speech mixed political and educational equality with endorsement of racial separation and race purity, so related answers are split. Tax rates and the tax bill's final form were set by Congress; he said he could not settle the tax debate for himself.
